items.name: Sky Garden
items.description: London's highest public garden with stunning 360° views. Free entry to the garden, with a bar and restaurant available. Book in advance.

items.name: Fabric
items.description: One of London's most legendary nightclubs, famous for its world-class DJs and incredible sound system. Three rooms of electronic music.

items.name: Ronnie Scott's Jazz Club
items.description: The world-famous jazz club that opened in 1959. Intimate venue with nightly performances from top jazz artists. Book tables in advance.

items.name: Madison Rooftop Bar
items.description: Stunning rooftop bar with panoramic views of St Paul's Cathedral and the London skyline. Great cocktails and a lively atmosphere.

items.name: XOYO
items.description: East London's favourite nightclub with a diverse music programme spanning house, techno, hip-hop and more. Three floors of music.

items.name: Aqua Nueva
items.description: Stunning Spanish restaurant and bar on the 5th floor with incredible views over London's West End. Perfect for cocktails before a night out.

items.name: Jazz Cafe Camden
items.description: Iconic Camden venue hosting live jazz, soul, hip-hop and world music. Great balcony views of the stage and a buzzing atmosphere.

items.name: EGG London
items.description: Massive nightclub venue near Kings Cross with indoor and outdoor spaces. Known for all-night and all-day events with top electronic music acts.

items.name: Cirque le Soir
items.description: Theatrical circus-themed nightclub in Soho — famous for celebrity sightings, extravagant performers and an electric party atmosphere until late.

items.name: Annabel's
items.description: London's most exclusive private members' club — decadent Mayfair townhouse with live music, incredible interiors and A-list clientele.

items.name: Heaven
items.description: Iconic LGBTQ+ superclub under the arches at Charing Cross. Legendary for its Thursday and Saturday nights with huge sound systems.

items.name: The Connaught Bar
items.description: Consistently ranked one of the world's best bars. Art deco elegance, legendary martini trolley, impeccable service in Mayfair.

items.name: The Lab Soho
items.description: Legendary cocktail bar credited with sparking London's cocktail renaissance. Inventive drinks in an intimate basement setting.

items.name: Café de Paris
items.description: Historic 1920s ballroom turned nightclub near Piccadilly Circus. Ornate glamour with a sweeping staircase and regular themed nights.

items.name: Swift Soho
items.description: Award-winning whisky and cocktail bar spread across two floors — upstairs relaxed, downstairs late-night party vibes.

items.name: The Box Soho
items.description: Cult members' club known for wild cabaret performances and celebrity regulars. One of London's most talked-about nightlife spots.

items.name: Radio Rooftop Bar
items.description: One of London's highest rooftop bars with 360° views across the city skyline from the ME Hotel. Great cocktails, stunning sunset views.

items.name: Coq d'Argent
items.description: Rooftop restaurant and bar in the heart of the City with a beautiful garden terrace above Bank junction. French cuisine with skyline views.

items.name: Netil360
items.description: Laid-back East London rooftop with panoramic views, less touristy than central options. Great for sunset drinks with a local crowd.

items.name: 100 Club
items.description: Legendary underground music venue that's hosted The Rolling Stones, Sex Pistols and countless icons since 1942. Jazz, punk, and everything between.

items.name: The Roundhouse
items.description: Iconic circular venue in a converted Victorian railway shed, hosting major concerts and performances across all genres.

items.name: Royal Albert Hall
items.description: One of the world's most famous concert venues — stunning Victorian architecture hosting classical, rock, and everything in between including the BBC Proms.

items.name: The George Fitzrovia
items.description: Named London Pub & Bar of the Year at the 2026 National Pub and Bar Awards — an upmarket boozer with real character.

items.name: Café Kick
items.description: Time Out's #1 best bar in London for 2026 — described as 'the Spanish Riviera and old school east London had a baby.' A five-star Exmouth Market institution.

items.name: Waltz
items.description: Crowned Time Out's Best Cocktail Bar in London for 2026 — inventive drinks in one of Shoreditch's most talked-about spaces.

items.name: Ellie's
items.description: Time Out's Best Neighbourhood Bar in London for 2026 — the kind of local spot regulars are fiercely loyal to.

items.name: Bonne Route
items.description: Time Out's highest-ranked wine bar in London for 2026 — an extensive by-the-glass list in a relaxed, unpretentious setting.

items.name: Tramps
items.description: Time Out's Best New Bar in London for 2026 — opened by acclaimed artist Peter Doig and gallerist Parinaz Mogadassi.

items.name: Scarfes Bar
items.description: A sweeping, grand hotel bar at the Rosewood London — vintage New York glamour with white-jacketed bartenders serving ice-cold martinis.

items.name: The Pelican
items.description: Posh Notting Hill gastropub shortlisted for the 2026 National Pub & Bar Awards — elegant food and a proper pub atmosphere.

items.name: The Orange
items.description: Elegant Belgravia pub-with-rooms shortlisted for the 2026 National Pub & Bar Awards — a proper local with polish.

items.name: Blue Stoops
items.description: Winner at the CAMRA Pub Design Awards 2026 — a beautifully refurbished former wine rooms with striking ceramic bar and modern fixtures.

items.name: Queen Elizabeth Hall Roof Garden
items.description: Time Out's #1 rooftop bar in London for 2026 — botany-inspired cocktails, craft beers and a sprawling green space started as a homelessness/addiction recovery gardening project.

items.name: Frank's Cafe
items.description: Time Out's #2 rooftop bar for 2026 — a beloved London institution atop a multi-storey car park, famous for its pink staircase, art installations and casual energy.

items.name: Forza Wine at The National Theatre
items.description: Time Out's #3 rooftop bar for 2026 — a wine-focused terrace on the top floor of the National Theatre, open year-round with river views.

items.name: Sushisamba City
items.description: The highest outdoor dining terraces in Europe, on the 39th floor of 110 Bishopsgate — Japanese-Peruvian-Brazilian fusion with 360° city views.

items.name: Queen of Hoxton
items.description: An ever-changing bar, club and rooftop across multiple floors — a Shoreditch nightlife staple with regular themed events.

items.name: Roof East
items.description: An 'adult adventure playground' atop a multi-storey car park — lawn bowls, crazy golf, London's highest baseball batting cage, street food and cocktail bars.

items.name: Savage Garden
items.description: Billed as London's wildest rooftop bar — bold jungle-inspired design and a lively party atmosphere in the heart of the City.

items.name: St Martin's Theatre
items.description: Home to The Mousetrap, the world's longest-running play, continuously staged since 1952 — an essential piece of London theatre history.

items.name: Palace Theatre
items.description: Home to Harry Potter and the Cursed Child — a stunning Victorian theatre in the heart of Theatreland showing the eighth Harry Potter story.

items.name: Lyceum Theatre
items.description: Long-running home of Disney's The Lion King — spectacular puppetry and staging near Covent Garden.

items.name: The Comedy Store
items.description: London's original and most famous stand-up comedy club since 1979 — home of the legendary Comedy Store Players improv troupe.

items.name: West End Comedy Club
items.description: A buzzing club in the heart of Theatreland featuring top TV comedians and rising stars — great for a fun night out with friends or family.

items.name: Regent's Park Open Air Theatre
items.description: A magical outdoor theatre inside Regent's Park — summer performances of musicals and classics under the stars, a genuinely unique London experience.

items.name: Ministry of Sound
items.description: London's most iconic superclub, running since 1991 with a legendary sound system and multi-room layout. A rite of passage for house and techno fans, with resident and headline DJs most weekends.
items.opinion: Loud, sweaty, and exactly what a London superclub should be — go for a big headline night, not a quiet one.

items.name: E1
items.description: A cavernous former warehouse turned cutting-edge club with an immersive sound and visual setup. One of East London's most talked-about openings for electronic music fans.
items.opinion: The production quality here is a step above most London clubs — worth the trek east.

items.name: 93 Feet East
items.description: A Brick Lane institution with an industrial courtyard and indoor stage that's hosted everyone from Radiohead to Burial. Regular house, techno, garage and disco nights in a relaxed East End setting.
items.opinion: Great outdoor courtyard for warm nights — check the lineup, the crowd shifts a lot by night.

items.name: Village Underground
items.description: A converted Victorian warehouse and railway carriages perched above Shoreditch, hosting both live gigs and club nights. Known for its distinctive rooftop carriages visible from the street below.
items.opinion: Check what's on — it swings between gigs and full club nights, so the vibe varies night to night.

items.name: Colours Hoxton
items.description: A multi-arts venue with a striking LED ceiling installation and a strong focus on inclusive, LGBTQ+-friendly programming, including the popular Pxssy Palace nights. House, techno and disco keep the floor moving late.
items.opinion: One of the more welcoming club spaces in Shoreditch — the LED ceiling alone is worth seeing.

items.name: Basing House
items.description: An intimate 300-capacity electronic music club open primarily Friday and Saturday nights, with a history of hosting respected underground house and techno acts since 2010.
items.opinion: Small and unpretentious — one of the better spots if you want music over spectacle.

items.name: Corsica Studios
items.description: A no-frills railway-arch club respected by serious electronic music heads for its bookings and sound system over polish. A go-to for underground house, techno and experimental line-ups.
items.opinion: Come for the music, not the décor — regulars will tell you that's exactly the point.

items.name: Studio 338
items.description: One of London's largest club spaces, set in a converted riverside industrial unit with a huge outdoor terrace. Known for marathon day-into-night sessions and major electronic music line-ups.
items.opinion: The outdoor terrace overlooking the river makes this one of the better summer clubbing spots in London.

items.name: FOLD
items.description: A purpose-built techno venue known for its immersive sound system and a loyal following of serious electronic music fans. One of the most respected underground clubs in East London.
items.opinion: Sound quality here is a cut above most London clubs — go for the music, not the aesthetics.

items.name: The Carpet Shop
items.description: A former carpet shop turned intimate club with a stripped-back dancefloor and a four-point Funktion-One sound system, from the team behind Corsica Studios.
items.opinion: Small, loud, and unflashy — one of the better new openings in South London.

items.name: Dalston Superstore
items.description: A cornerstone of queer nightlife since 2009, blending club nights, cabaret, and a proudly inclusive community spirit across two floors.
items.opinion: One of East London's most consistently welcoming and fun nights out.

items.name: Colour Factory
items.description: A large indoor-outdoor venue anchoring summer programming in East London's canal-side creative quarter, with capacity up to 1,800 depending on event format.
items.opinion: Best experienced in summer when the outdoor space is in full use.

items.name: Venue MOT
items.description: A no-frills warehouse space respected within London's underground electronic scene for serious, community-driven bookings over spectacle.
items.opinion: Not the easiest to find, but that's part of the appeal for regulars.

items.name: The Cause
items.description: A community-focused warehouse venue in North London running day-into-night sessions with a strong reputation among techno and house purists.
items.opinion: Runs some of the longest, most committed daytime-into-night sessions in London.

items.name: Phonox
items.description: A Brixton institution known for a rotating residency programme featuring some of the world's most respected house and disco DJs, in a low-ceilinged, intimate basement space.
items.opinion: The residency line-ups here are consistently some of the strongest bookings in London.

items.name: NT's Loft
items.description: A rooftop bar and club with skyline views, laid-back by day and energetic by night. Regularly hosts funk, soul, house and disco alongside live performances and good pizza.
items.opinion: Great for a sunset drink that turns into a full night out.

items.name: KOKO
items.description: A lavishly restored Grade II-listed Camden theatre blending old-world grandeur with a forward-thinking music programme spanning electronic acts and high-profile live shows.
items.opinion: One of the most beautiful venues in London — worth going just to see the room.

items.name: Drumsheds
items.description: A vast 14,999-capacity warehouse venue in North London hosting some of the biggest electronic music line-ups in the city, ranked among the world's top clubs.
items.opinion: A genuine spectacle-scale venue — book early for headline nights.

items.name: Electrowerkz
items.description: A gritty, multi-room venue long associated with goth, industrial and electronic subcultures, including the long-running Slimelight night — one of London's longest-running alternative club nights.
items.opinion: Not for everyone — but a genuine slice of London's alternative club history.

items.name: Eutopia Warehouse
items.description: An East London warehouse venue with a strong community-programming ethos, known for extended sessions and a loyal underground following.
items.opinion: Check the lineup carefully — programming varies significantly night to night.

items.name: Trapeze Bar
items.description: A Shoreditch venue combining live music and club nights across a huge range of genres — rock, indie, electronic, hip-hop, punk and metal — with a packed weekly events calendar.
items.opinion: Great if you want variety — the programming genuinely spans every genre.

items.name: Bussey Building
items.description: A converted Victorian warehouse and Peckham nightlife institution, hosting club nights, live music and a rooftop bar across multiple spaces.
items.opinion: One of Peckham's original nightlife anchors — still going strong.

items.name: JUMBI
items.description: A hi-fi bar from Rhythm Section boss Bradley Zero, where dancing is practically compulsory. A Peckham favourite for disco, soul and dance-focused sets.
items.opinion: Small, sound-focused, and one of the friendliest dancefloors in South London.

items.name: Printworks
items.description: A former newspaper printing facility turned one of London's most visually striking large-scale club venues, hosting major international electronic acts across cavernous industrial rooms.
items.opinion: The scale and production of this venue is unlike anywhere else in London.

items.name: Night Tales
items.description: A multi-space venue with an outdoor terrace and indoor club room, popular for group nights out and special occasions with a broad, crowd-pleasing music policy.
items.opinion: Good option if your group has mixed music tastes — the programming is broad.

items.name: The Pickle Factory
items.description: An intimate East London venue with a strong reputation for underground electronic bookings in a compact, sweaty setting.
items.opinion: Small capacity means it sells out fast for good line-ups — book early.

items.name: Ormside Projects
items.description: A creative warehouse space combining gallery exhibitions with club nights, popular among London's more experimental electronic music crowd.
items.opinion: Part gallery, part club — worth checking what's on before you go.

items.name: Slimelight
items.description: One of London's longest-running goth and industrial-electronic club nights, held at Electrowerkz since the early 1990s — a genuine piece of alternative club history.
items.opinion: A cult institution — go once even if it's not your usual scene.
